scope: Every phase 2 case with prompt version 7 (257 of 584): the flow operation, reference, predicate and branch export fixtures, the public v7 examples and the 230 v7 legacy jobs. All 257 ran in one check_phase2.py --language rust run on the binary above.

behavior.method: check_phase2.py run --language rust --qa http://127.0.0.1:18956 --only <257 v7 ids> on a dev server of the binary above (dev-k-001). Each case compiles the typed JSON prompt with target rust, assembles, builds the product with the pinned toolchain and runs the flow checker: core flow, generated tests, branch coverage, owner checks, database and provider fault injection on every step with undo, lease and restart checks.

clippy_sweep.note: One product per distinct rust.files_sha256 of flow-full-001.

product_checks.som_targets: cargo clippy -D warnings and cargo test (20 passed) passed on som-rs/som-targets at 9e3df2e119. cargo fmt --check did not pass at 9e3df2e119 (src/rust/mod.rs tests and render/capability/flow.rs were not formatted; an earlier check filtered its output). The next commit formats them and passes cargo fmt --check, clippy and cargo test.
product_checks.follow_up: A #55 dry run found that the PostgreSQL flow migrations put the columns in another order than the Python flow model (schema_equivalence compares ordinal order). The next commit orders them as Python (id, _som_revision, created_at, updated_at, fields, foreign key); the products decode rows by name, so behavior does not depend on it. The #55 run checks every flow product with the fixed binary.
not_run: phase 2 bundle_checks: CNL and JSON byte-identical bundles, determinism, layout and reference Cargo files (#55)
phase 2 product_gates: cargo test on a fresh database, Cargo.lock unchanged, schema and index equivalence with the Python product (#55)
each product's own cargo test (the sweep compiles the tests with --no-run)

known_differences: -0.0: the bundle and the generated FLOW literal keep the sign of zero; the PostgreSQL journal stores JSONB, which drops the sign, as the Python flow product does.
